observation: Bengaluru has the highest median asking price (₹13,227,000), 15.8% above the lowest-priced city, Chennai (₹11,418,000).
evidence: segmentation.segment_by_city() — SQL GROUP BY over 8000 properties across 6 cities.
business_implication: City-level price dispersion is moderate (not extreme), suggesting the dataset doesn't have one dominant 'hot market' city — investment opportunity is more locality-driven than city-driven.
recommended_action: Prioritize locality-level analysis (not just city) when screening investment opportunities.
confidence: high — based on full-population SQL aggregation, not a sample

observation: Property type is NOT a statistically significant driver of price (Kruskal-Wallis p=0.097), explaining only 0.1% of price variance.
business_implication: Counter-intuitive: in this dataset, AREA (sqft) drives price far more than the property TYPE label (Apartment vs Villa vs Studio) — consistent with the strong area<->price correlation (r=0.837, see Insight 4).
recommended_action: Valuation models should weight area_sqft heavily and treat property_type as a secondary feature — consistent with what src/ml_valuation_model.py already found (area_sqft = 0.84 feature importance).
confidence: high — p-value and effect size both point the same direction

observation: 8.34% of transactions are IQR-flagged as price outliers, traced to a runaway monthly-compounding bug in the price-growth formula — national avg price/sqft grew 10,818→51,141 (2020→2025), a statistically extreme YoY +90.8% in the final year alone.
evidence: outliers.analyze_transaction_price_outliers() [1668 IQR outliers] + time_series national trend [year-over-year 2020:10818.56 -> 2025:51141.74] + distributions.py [price_per_sqft skewness=12.2, excess_kurtosis=172]
business_implication: ML models trained on transaction_price-derived features (or a future model using raw transaction price as a target) would learn this runaway trend as real signal — a genuine leakage/bias risk for any model trained on the full 2020-2025 window without correction.
recommended_action: FIX AT SOURCE in Phase 3+: add a growth ceiling/mean-reversion term to the locality price-growth formula in data/generate_data_part2.py. Until fixed, prefer market_monthly.average_price_sqft (same bug, but at least aggregated) over raw transaction_price for any new model.
confidence: high — root cause traced to specific line of generator code, reproducible

observation: area_sqft has the strongest correlation with asking_price of any feature pair (Pearson r=0.838).
evidence: correlations.run_full_correlation_analysis()['property_level']['top_pearson']. Correlation does not imply causation — but area is a direct multiplicative input to price by construction in the generator, so this is expected, not spurious.
business_implication: Confirms the valuation model's heavy reliance on area_sqft (84% feature importance) is well-founded, not an artifact of an under-featured model.
recommended_action: No action needed — this validates existing ML model design (src/ml_valuation_model.py).
confidence: high — consistent with known data-generation logic

observation: Sampath Constructions leads sales velocity at 93.3% (rating 4.9), vs Borra Constructions at only 68.3% (rating 2.0).
evidence: segmentation.segment_by_developer() — analytics.v_developer_performance view, filtered to developers with >=3 projects.
business_implication: Developer quality/delivery track record (correlated with rating by construction) is a meaningful differentiator in absorption — relevant to the Decision Engine's market_score component.
recommended_action: Decision Engine already incorporates developer signal indirectly via risk scoring — consider adding sales_velocity_pct as an explicit Decision Engine input in a future calibration phase.
confidence: medium — descriptive, not yet hypothesis-tested for statistical significance

observation: Interest rate shows essentially zero correlation with demand_index in the cross-sectional data (Pearson r=-0.004, p=0.73, not significant) despite the data generator's formula explicitly reducing demand as interest rates rise.
business_implication: The interest-rate effect (coefficient -0.6 per point, see data/generate_data_part2.py) is small relative to other demand noise (std dev ~1.5/month) — it exists in the generator but is not statistically detectable in aggregate. A forecasting model would likely not find interest rate a useful demand predictor as currently generated.
recommended_action: If interest-rate sensitivity is meant to be a demonstrable feature of this platform, the generator's interest-rate coefficient should be strengthened in a future data-regeneration phase.
confidence: high — p-value directly measured, not inferred
